conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could forge or suppress keeper.err so software accepts a timed-out transaction or rejects a valid response.

conceptual assets.information: The halt decision suppresses timeout handling for the fallback target selected by the gateway. It has no direct port because it is an internal decision derived from target selection.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because keeper.halt is produced from the fallback selection at line 416 and suppresses the timeout-error branch at lines 423 and 424; availability is at risk because an incorrect suppression decision can prevent recovery from a stalled transaction.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force timeout suppression for a nonresponsive target, leaving the gateway busy indefinitely.

conceptual assets.information: The device-address decode selects which of the enabled device request ports receives the main bus transaction. It has no direct entry or exit port because the main request address only determines the internal per-device routing decisions.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because each device request strobe is selected by an address comparison at lines 661 through 664; availability is at risk because an altered comparison can prevent a request from reaching its intended device.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could change the decoded device target so accesses reach the wrong peripheral or are dropped.

conceptual assets.information: The atomic-operation command determines which read-modify-write function is performed and whether the operation is accepted. The operation-selector fields are part of this operation rather than a separate boundary asset.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the request command is captured at lines 777 and 778 and selects the ALU behavior at lines 838 through 845; availability is at risk because the same command acceptance test at line 777 can prevent an atomic operation from starting.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the atomic operation code to perform a different memory update or prevent the requested atomic operation from executing.

conceptual assets.information: The write operand supplied with an atomic request is held while the read-modify-write operation computes its update. The operand enters through core_req_i.data and is consumed by the internal atomic computation rather than returned unchanged.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because core_req_i.data is stored in arbiter.wdata at line 779 and can influence the externally visible update word at lines 839 through 843 and 813; integrity is at risk because changing the captured operand changes the atomic update.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could read or alter the captured operand, causing a confidential value to influence an unintended write or causing the atomic update to use attacker-chosen data.

conceptual assets.information: The value read from the system bus is held for the atomic computation and returned to the core as the prior memory value. It enters through sys_rsp_i.data and leaves through core_rsp_o.data.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because sys_rsp_i.data is captured at line 785 and returned through core_rsp_o.data at line 826; integrity is at risk because changing the captured value changes both the returned prior value and the computed atomic update.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe or replace the read value while it is held, exposing memory contents or causing the core to receive and use an incorrect prior value.

conceptual assets.information: The computed atomic update value is produced by the ALU from the held read value, write operand, and operation semantics, then sent to the system bus as write data. It is generated inside the unit and has no separate entry port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because alu_res is an internally computed data value exposed on sys_req_o.data at line 813; integrity is at risk because the ALU assignments at lines 839 through 845 directly determine the value written to the system bus.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the computed result so an atomic memory operation writes attacker-selected data or reveals information through the outgoing write word.

conceptual assets.information: The write-phase control determines when the computed atomic result is issued as a write rather than as the original request. It is an internal decision expressed at the sys_req_o.stb and sys_req_o.rw output fields.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because arbiter.state selects the outgoing write data, direction, and strobe at lines 813, 815, and 816; availability is at risk because corrupting these controls can suppress the write phase or issue it at the wrong time.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force or suppress the write-phase strobe, causing an atomic update to be omitted, duplicated, or issued as the wrong bus operation.

conceptual assets.information: The reservation state records whether a load-reserved operation established the condition required for a later store-conditional operation. The unit depends on it to permit or reject the conditional store.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because state is set and cleared by request and response conditions at lines 910 through 927 and determines whether a conditional store proceeds; availability is at risk because corrupting the reservation can permanently reject valid stores or allow the state machine to wait incorrectly.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could forge or clear the reservation so a store-conditional operation succeeds without a valid reservation or is rejected indefinitely.

conceptual assets.information: The conditional-store issue decision determines whether the store-conditional request is presented to the system bus after checking the operation type and reservation state. It leaves through sys_req_o.stb.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because rvso and state gate the outgoing store strobe at lines 943 through 946; availability is at risk because forcing the decision low blocks a valid conditional store while forcing it high can issue an unauthorized one.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could bypass the reservation check or suppress the outgoing strobe, respectively causing an invalid store or preventing a valid store.

conceptual assets.information: The conditional-store result reports whether the store-conditional failed and modifies the response returned to the core. It is produced internally and leaves through the response acknowledge and data fields.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because sc_fail is produced from the request and reservation state at line 957 and changes core_rsp_o.ack and core_rsp_o.data at lines 963 and 964.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could forge the conditional-store result so the core accepts a failed store or treats a successful store as failed.

considered, not kept.concept: Forwarded bus transactions and relayed data
considered, not kept.reason: The switch forwards request and response records between ports at lines 140 through 169 without storing or computing their ordinary data, so the Forwarded transactions rule bars them as concepts of this unit.
state only orders arbitration steps and is therefore barred as sequencing state; sel_q is also only previous-grant bookkeeping, as shown at lines 49 through 57 and 112.
locked only copies the lock bit of the access in progress and uses it to pass, time, or end that access at lines 51, 57, 88, 100, and 111, so bus-handshake copies bars it as an independent piece.

The gateway forwards request and response records through port_req, port_rsp, and int_rsp at lines 366 through 401; relayed transactions and merged responses are barred except for the separate routing and timeout decisions.
keeper.busy only tracks and times the current transaction and does not refuse a write or new command, so it is sequencing state rather than a busy lock under lines 417 through 429.
keeper.lock copies req_i.lock and only controls completion of the current bus access at lines 420 and 426, so it is barred as a bus-handshake copy.
The A_BASE, B_BASE, C_BASE, enable, and timeout generics are build-time values declared at lines 285 through 300 and cannot be changed at run time.

The request and response records are forwarded through the bus-reg instance and dev_req/dev_rsp paths at lines 608 through 690, so forwarded transactions and register stages are not concepts of this unit.
INREG_EN, OUTREG_EN, DEV_SIZE, device enables, and device bases are build-time generics and constants at lines 458 through 494 and 563 through 581.
arbiter.state only sequences the read, execute, write, and wait steps at lines 773 through 806, so the Sequencing state rule bars it as a separate concept.

considered, not kept.concept: RMW opcode as a separate piece

considered, not kept.reason: The ordinary request and response fields are forwarded at lines 942, 962, and 964, so relayed bus data and handshake are barred; only the reservation, issue decision, and conditional-store result are retained.

considered, not kept.concept: RVS operation-type flag as a separate piece

reply keys: the 2026-10-13 format as written in 'raw'; 'reply' holds it in v5 keys
